question: A closed right circular cylinder has total surface area $54\pi$ cm$^2$. Find its radius and height when its volume is maximum.
explanation:
Surface-area constraint
For radius $r$ and height $h$,
$$2\pi r^2+2\pi rh=54\pi$$
Therefore,
$$r^2+rh=27\Rightarrow h=\frac{27}{r}-r$$
Volume function
$$V=\pi r^2h=\pi r^2\left(\frac{27}{r}-r\right)$$
$$V=\pi(27r-r^3)$$
Stationary condition
$$V'(r)=\pi(27-3r^2)=0$$
Thus, $r=3$ cm.
Maximum verification
$$V''(r)=-6\pi r$$
Since $V''(3)<0$, the volume is maximum.
Height
$$h=\frac{27}{3}-3=6\text{ cm}$$
Conclusion
The required radius is $3$ cm and height is $6$ cm.
